steps.text: With Node.js and the CLI installed, create a workspace. This demo skips MCP setup.

Stop with Ctrl+C, then run primo dev --author cms to edit in the browser.

clips.title: Recover from a refused CLI push

steps.text: Pull from the server to record a baseline. Here PRIMO_SERVER points to an isolated local demo.
After a local code edit and a server edit, push refuses to overwrite the newer server version.
Save the edited file outside sites/, then pull the latest server copy.
Reapply the saved code edit and push again. The server change is preserved.
The pushed headline appears in the CMS. On a hosted server, review and Publish to update the public site.

clips.title: Deploy Primo on Railway with the CLI

steps.text: Create a Railway project. CLI commands in this walkthrough use the linked demo project and service.
Add an empty service for Primo.
Before deploying, attach persistent storage at /app/pb_data. Verify the mount path.
Configure Primo account variables privately. This excerpt hides passwords; normal variable output contains secrets.
Connect the service to the published Primo image. This demo pins the 3.3.1 image digest.
Wait for the service deployment to report SUCCESS. The waiting period is omitted here.
Generate a Railway hostname on port 8080. Railway supplies DNS routing and HTTPS for this address.
Open /admin/dashboard over HTTPS. Sign in with the regular Primo account, not the PocketBase superuser.
The fresh CMS is ready for sites. Credential entry is omitted from this recording.
Garden Studio is prepared fictional demo content, imported off camera.
Save a visible headline change before testing a redeployment.
Redeploy the same service with the same volume. Deployment waiting is omitted.
Reload the editor. The headline survives; all 37 exported files match the pre-redeployment copy.

clips.title: Connect a Railway hostname and publish a site

steps.text: Use the Railway-generated hostname. Its DNS routing and HTTPS are already configured by Railway.
The prepared site begins without a public hostname assigned in Primo.
Open the site menu and choose Assign domain.
Enter the Railway hostname without https:// or a path, then choose Connect.
For this generated Railway hostname, skip registrar DNS steps: routing and HTTPS are already verified.
Mark as connected records manual connection status. It does not publish the site.
Open the editor and choose Publish. Confirm the destination, then choose Publish changes.
Wait for Changes published before viewing the public site.
Open the public HTTPS homepage and verify the saved headline.
Follow a navigation link and verify the About page.
Check a nested blog URL too. This walkthrough uses a Railway hostname; custom domains also need your own DNS configuration.
